A.lawCode: Amd §65-b, ABC L; amd §§851 & 855, Cor L; amd §3-0301, En Con L; amd §261, Exec L; amd §3.09, Pks & Rec L; amd §1198, V & T L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A1801A

TITLE  OF BILL:  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, the
correction law, the environmental conservation law, the  executive  law,
the  parks, recreation and historic preservation law and the vehicle and
traffic law, in relation to compensatory service

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:   This  bill  would  change  "community
service"  to  "compensatory  service"  in certain alternative sentencing
programs.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:  Section 1 of the bill amends paragraphs
(a), (b), and (c) of subdivision 4 of  section  65-b  of  the  alcoholic
beverage  control  law  to  replace "community service" to "compensatory
service" as a penalty for violation of the article.

Section 2 of the bill amends paragraphs (a), (b), and (c) of subdivision
2 and subdivision 3 of section 65-b of the  alcoholic  beverage  control
law to replace "community service" to "compensatory service" as a penal-
ty for violation of the article.

Section  3  of  the  bill  amends  subdivision  5  of section 851 of the
correction law to replace "community service program" with "compensatory
services program" for eligible inmates to participate  in  off  premises
service related activities.

Section  4  of  the  bill  amends  subdivision  2  of section 855 of the
correction law to replace "community services program" with "compensato-
ry services program".

Section 5 of the bill amends paragraph hit of subdivision 1  of  section
3-0301  of  the  environmental  conservation  law  to replace "community
service" with "compensatory service".

Section 6 of the bill amends paragraph b of subdivision I of section 261
of the executive law to replace "community service"  with  "compensatory
service".

Section  7  of  the  bill  amends subdivision 2-f of section 3.09 of the
parks, recreation, and historic preservation law to  replace  "community
service" with "compensatory service".

Section  8  of the bill amends paragraph (e) of subdivision 3 of section
1198 of the vehicle and traffic law to replace "community service"  with
"compensatory service".

Section 9 of the bill provides for an effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:    This  bill  would replace the term "community service'
with "compensatory service." Presently, Justices  throughout  our  state
often  impose community service sentences in lieu of paying fines or, in
some cases, serving jail time.  This  term  implies  an  aura  of  civic

responsibility,  as most who perform community service do so voluntarily
and out of kindness.

The criminal defendant, on the other hand, is mandated to contribute his
or  her  time to community programs in lieu of paying a fine or going to
jail. It is extremely doubtful that many of those presently sentenced to
"community service" would do such work on  their  own  without  a  Court
mandate. Their actions therefore should be given a different terminology
than those who voluntarily perform community service.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2007-2008: A.3882- Passed both houses, Veto No. 66
2005-2006: A.1254/S.6991- Passed Both Houses, Veto No. 244
2003-2004: A.5118- Passed Assembly/ S.2576- Committed to Rules
2001-2002: A.336-A- Passed Assembly) S.7601- Referred to Rules

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Changes community service to be compensatory service in certain sentencing alternative programs to distinguish such service from the service provided by volunteers.
